clue.text: Fury about broadcast includes Question Time, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for fury goes around the other letters, so it surrounds them

parts.note: fury is violent passion or rage

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a rage about broadcasting includes a well-known BBC programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles to NELDISCU, which 'about' places inside the word for fury. Question Time is a BBC TV programme where a panel answers audience questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Question Time is an example: a televised debate in which a panel of public figures answers questions.

clue.text: Reformed pioneers sang about the virgin birth

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the word given, holding it inside
reformed means formed again, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Religious reformers sing hymns about the Virgin Birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' gives PARNOGENESIS, which 'about' splits after its third letter to hold the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists use this term for reproduction from an unfertilised egg, literally a virgin birth.

clue.text: Prayers left out of book on Spanish saint's upbringing

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for book

parts.note: a novel is a book

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a word reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: San is the Spanish title for a saint; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: A child's upbringing involves prayers omitted from a book about a Spanish saint.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVEL loses L to give NOVE; 'upbringing' turns SAN upwards to NAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A novena is a Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine successive days.

clue.text: Laid-back learner initially exasperated instructor, no doubt

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: no doubt means surely, certainly

explanation.surface: A relaxed learner driver initially exasperates the driving instructor, without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe an unhurried, relaxed manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Old pub, it's said, was furnished with metal bar

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than written, so only its sound counts

parts.note: an inn is an old-fashioned name for a pub
was furnished with means got, received

explanation.surface: An old pub, the story goes, was furnished with a metal bar.
explanation.walkthrough: INN sounds like IN, which is added to GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, often gold, shaped like a bar.

clue.text: Phoney map outlines the French-Algerian borders

indicators.note: the word for map outlines, goes around, the French article

parts.note: a chart is a map
la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: borders are the edges, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A fake map outlines the border between France and Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney as a noun means a fraud, an impostor pretending to skills he lacks.

clue.text: Knight taken in by soothsayer's superior look

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a seer is a soothsayer, a prophet; the 's stands for is
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is deceived by a fortune-teller with a haughty expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like 'fooled', but here it means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemptuous expression, a curled lip, is a superior look.

clue.text: International tech company set up foundation for drunk

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: IBM is the American computing company
a bed is a foundation, as in a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: A global technology firm establishes a charity for alcoholics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IBM into MBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk as a past participle means consumed as liquid, which is a synonym of imbibed.

clue.text: New clue: carrots are alternative sources of energy

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters of the clue words before it gives a different order

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter suggests carrots as a form of renewable energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' scrambles the three clue words into UCLEARREACTORS. 'alternative sources of energy' wants to be the definition, but alternative is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Power stations generate electricity from nuclear fission inside these devices.

clue.text: Increasing power of engine, one's excluded from rallying

indicators.note: the letter is left out of the longer word

parts.note: rallying means reviving, recovering
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: In motor rallying a single driver is disqualified for gunning the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rallying' suggests motor sport, which fits the engine, but means recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising an engine's speed by pressing the throttle is the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Tip of red pen used by card sharp

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter of the word

parts.note: Bic is a famous brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A card sharp uses the point of a red pen to mark cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card sharp' reads as a cheat, but sharp is the definition and card is ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic remarks are sharp, biting and sour in tone.

clue.text: Religious type joins church in Dublin

indicators.note: the letters run across the joins between these words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A believer joins a church in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the main religion of India is this, a type of religious believer.

clue.text: Mediocre line in Lear to be rewritten

indicators.note: the letter for line goes into the rearranged letters
rewritten text is reworked, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A weak line in King Lear needs rewriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' reshuffles LEAR TO BE, and 'in' puts L among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something merely passable, neither good nor bad, is mediocre, an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Soldiers' lodgings in Northern Ireland closed? About three-quarters

indicators.note: the word for closed goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: closed means shut
the compass has four quarters; south, east and north are three of them

explanation.surface: Army barracks in Northern Ireland have been closed, perhaps around three-quarters of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters' looks like a fraction but means three compass points, S, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: These semicircular corrugated-iron huts were used as quick-built barracks for troops.

clue.text: Home Office suppresses independent survey on Love Island and Plebs

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of the next holds it down

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK interior ministry
a poll is a survey of opinion
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: The Home Office buries an independent survey on the reality show Love Island and the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British TV dating show.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek phrase for the many, used in English for the common people.

clue.text: Greeting communist revolutionary; one who's on the run?

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A communist revolutionary on the run greets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'communist revolutionary' reads as a radical, but 'revolutionary' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive hides from pursuers, so someone on the run is one who hides.

clue.text: Deborah, wandering around ancient city, found shelter

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the city's name
wandering letters stray from their places into a new order

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Deborah wandered round an ancient city and found a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' gives HARBOED, which 'around' opens after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking refuge, as a ship does in port, is the intransitive sense of this past tense verb.

clue.text: An abandoned part of Europe, crawling with bugs

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Germany is a country, a part of Europe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deserted region of Europe is infested with insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bugs' suggests insects; here they are microbes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs informally means germs, so something crawling with them is full of microbes.

clue.text: Nice surroundings

parts.note: Nice is the French city, and the coastline around it is the French Mediterranean resort coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The French resort coast where the city of Nice stands is the region surrounding it.

clue.text: Crossing Tiber with nun, cardinal produces rubber ring

indicators.note: crossing lines are criss-crossed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: E, east, is one of the cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A nun and a cardinal cross the Tiber in Rome, one of them using a rubber ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' rearranges TIBER and NUN to give INNERTUB. 'cardinal' looks like the churchman but is East.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable tube inside a tyre doubles as a swimming float, a rubber ring.

clue.text: Separate organisation has duplicate key

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations organisation
a twin is a duplicate
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An organisation splits up, holding a spare key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like something for a lock; it is the musical key E.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwist strands that were wound together is to separate them.

clue.text: Message delivered by raven is not to be repeated

definitions.meaning: the refrain croaked by the bird in Poe's poem The Raven
never again, never to happen another time

explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Allan Poe's poem has the raven repeat one word as its refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the raven's refrain in Poe's poem and also a poetic word meaning never again.

clue.text: Initially, radiology expert noted acute lesions of the kidneys

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: At first a radiologist found sharp lesions on the kidneys.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective, from Latin for kidney, means relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: Journalist claiming award is fix

indicators.note: the journalist claims, holds, the award inside

parts.note: ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A reporter claims an honour is rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' looks like a rigged result, but it is the verb, set firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something firmly into a surrounding mass is to fix it there.

clue.text: Measure introduced to stop bottlenecks?

parts.note: reads like traffic policy, but describes a pub device fitted into the neck of an upturned spirits bottle to dispense a measure

explanation.walkthrough: 'bottlenecks' suggests traffic jams; the device actually sits in the necks of bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: In British bars this device, fitted to an inverted bottle, dispenses a fixed measure of spirits.

clue.text: Starts to remove needle lodged within half-inch of breastbone

indicators.note: the picked letters are lodged inside the word for steal

parts.note: half-inch is rhyming slang for pinch, meaning steal

indicators.note: starts points to the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A surgeon begins removing a needle lodged in the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-inch' is Cockney rhyming slang: half-inch rhymes with pinch, so it means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: This anatomical adjective means relating to the sternum, the breastbone.

clue.text: Food, back massage and joint in Brazilian city

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to massage

indicators.note: the letter goes in the city's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city
a T-joint is a T-shaped joint in plumbing

explanation.surface: A holiday in Brazil: food, a back massage and a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back massage' reads as a treatment, but 'back' reverses RUB. 'joint' is the T-shaped pipe joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican dish of a tortilla wrapped around a filling is an item of food.

clue.text: South precinct was troubled by lawman's petty attitude

parts.note: a shopping precinct is a mall
to have minded something is to have been bothered by it
Eliot Ness was the US lawman who led the Untouchables; the 's links him to what follows

explanation.surface: A southern police precinct was troubled by an officer's narrow-minded attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precinct' suggests a police station, but here it is a shopping precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowness of outlook and pettiness in judgement are what this noun describes.
